kitDescription: Milk (Treasure) is a Water SR Burst-I Attacker whose treasure rework makes her a fast-cycling team buffer. Every 20 seconds she grants the three highest-final-ATK allies (herself eligible) +31.83% ATK for 10 seconds, and her own Burst cooldown is permanently shortened from 40s to 20s, letting her cast every rotation. While she stays above 80% HP the whole team gets +11.13% Critical Damage, and every 10th full-charge shot refunds 2.83 seconds of Burst cooldown for all allies, accelerating the team's Full Burst cycle. Her Burst deals 367.34% of final ATK to the highest-DEF enemy and heals all allies over 10 seconds (with +75.5% incoming healing, unmodelable in the sim). She is a 20-second-cadence Burst I whose main value is rotation acceleration plus team ATK/crit support.

verdictRationale: No real gotchas. All six modeled lines are FAITHFUL and the seventh (incoming healing) is a triply-converged DOCUMENTED_GAP; every encoding was independently re-derived block-for-block by S6 and disposition-matched by S2b, with the sole substantive divergence — S6's one-shot burstCdr for the 'continuously' self-CDR — being a disclosed blind-side risk-posture misread that the kit's own grammar contrast (K2 '▼20s continuously' vs K4's bare '▼2.83s'), S2b's independent ruling, and the engine's channel mechanics all resolve in the driver's favor. The pristine S5 run shows 3 RED assertions, but both failure classes are blind-side mechanical artifacts (a no-op counterfactual patch against the charFixes channel; a reader filtering a non-existent per-unit event array), and the intent-preserved adapted copy is 23/0/4 GREEN — the driver's own spec independently proves the same semantics (11 vs 8 casts, gap-sign split at 20s). Discrimination is real throughout: treasure 3-vs-2 scope, static-vs-final-ATK ranking, self-vs-team crit damage, K4 removal moving the whole rotation, burstCast-vs-fullBurstEnter via the FB-major flag, and instant-vs-10-tick heal under a clean isolation fixture. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: (1) the K2 permanent-CD reading rests on grammar convergence among same-family agents — a single in-game cast-cadence check (milk bursting on ~20s cycles) would close it from independent evidence; (2) the chargeCounter-vs-hitCount identity is unprovable on this unit under current SR auto-play and is pinned by encoding alone; (3) the interval first-fire phase (t=20 vs t=0) is the standing ⚑ convention. None of these block GO.
